note: Prepared from the unit title and the trade's usual practice. An instructor must read and correct it, and mark it Ready, before it is opened for an intake.

unit.title: Install and maintain electronic electrical equipment and distribution circuits

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: A garment factory in Kingston will have a variable speed drive (VSD) fitted to a 3.7 kW fan motor. What should you read before planning the installation?
options: The fan maker's sales brochure and price list only
The drive maker's installation manual and the motor nameplate
The invoice left by the electrician who last worked on the fan
The building's plumbing and drainage drawings

questions.stem: A 4-pole motor fed by a VSD at 50 Hz has a synchronous speed of 1 500 rpm. About what will its synchronous speed be at 25 Hz?
options: 3 000 rpm
1 500 rpm
375 rpm
750 rpm

questions.stem: A 2-pole motor is fed at 50 Hz. Using n = 120 × f ÷ p, what is its synchronous speed?
options: 3 000 rpm
1 500 rpm
6 000 rpm
1 000 rpm

questions.stem: A VSD slows a fan to 80% of its full speed. Fan power varies roughly with speed cubed. About what share of full power does the fan now need?
Why does a VSD maker ask for a screened (shielded) cable between the drive and the motor?
options: So that the motor can run at a higher speed than its rating
So that no protective earth conductor is needed at all
To reduce electrical noise reaching other equipment
So that the cable can be run without any fixings

questions.stem: How is the screen of a VSD motor cable usually terminated, as most drive makers say?
options: Clamped all round in an EMC gland or clamp, at both ends
Twisted into a long pigtail and left unconnected at the motor
Cut back and taped over at both ends of the cable
Connected to the neutral bar inside the panel

questions.stem: Why are VSD motor cables run apart from control and data cables?
options: So that the motor cable stays cooler
So that the motor cable can be thinner
So the control cables need no screens
Fast switching can disturb nearby cables

questions.stem: An insulation resistance test is needed on a motor and its cable, which are fed from a VSD. What must be done first, with everything isolated?
options: Leave the drive connected so that it is tested as well
Disconnect the cable from the drive's output terminals
Set the drive's speed to its lowest value
Take off the motor's protective earth connection

questions.stem: A VSD is to be mounted in a panel. Why does the maker give a minimum space above and below it?
options: So cooling air can flow through its heatsink
So its display can be read from across the room
So the drive can be lifted out with one hand
So other drives can be stacked on it later

questions.stem: A VSD will be installed in a hot plant room where the air reaches 45 °C. What does the maker's data usually tell you to do?
options: Fit it anyway, as drives work better in the heat
Run the motor at a higher frequency to cool it
Derate the drive or improve the cooling
Remove the drive's own fan to save energy

questions.stem: After a VSD is installed and dead-tested, who sets its parameters (motor data, ramp times, limits)?
options: Any trainee, by trying values until the motor runs
The authorised person, from the nameplate and the manual
The fan supplier, talking you through it by telephone while it is live
Nobody, as drives work correctly without any settings

questions.stem: What is the main job of a soft starter on a pump motor?
options: To vary the motor's running speed throughout the day
To change a single-phase supply into three-phase
To take the place of the motor's overload protection
To ramp the voltage up gently and cut starting current

questions.stem: Many soft starters have a bypass contactor that closes once the motor is up to speed. Why?
options: To make the motor run faster than its rated speed
To let the motor run with no overload protection
To make the motor start more quickly each time
To cut heat losses in the starter while running

questions.stem: A spare controller input card arrives in a sealed silver-grey anti-static bag. When should it be taken out?
options: As soon as it arrives, so the store can check it in
At the panel, with ESD precautions, just before fitting
In the van on the way to site, so that it is ready
Never, because the card is designed to be fitted still inside its bag

questions.stem: A 24 V DC control supply must feed loads that total 1.6 A. Which power supply is the best choice?
options: 24 V, 1.6 A exactly

questions.stem: Why must the earth terminal of a switch-mode power supply in a metal panel be connected?
options: Its filter and case need an earth for safety and noise
So that its output can be raised from 24 V to 48 V
So that the supply can run safely without any fuse
So that the panel door can be opened while it is live

questions.stem: The status window on a surge protective device (SPD) in a board has changed from green to red. What does this usually mean?
options: It is working well and has just stopped a surge
It has reached the end of its life and must be replaced
The board is overloaded and must be split into two
The earth rod outside needs to be watered

questions.stem: Why is surge protection often fitted at the main board and again close to sensitive equipment?
options: Each stage lowers the surge further
A single SPD is never allowed on its own
The second SPD is needed to trip the first
SPDs only work when two are fitted in series

questions.stem: An office has many computers and LED drivers on a three-phase supply. Why might its neutral run hot even when the line currents are balanced?
options: Electronic loads always draw less current than lamps do
Computers send their return current through the earth
LED drivers stop any current from flowing in the neutral
Distorted currents from electronic loads add up in the neutral

questions.stem: During a power cut, what should a grid-tied solar inverter do, as it is designed to?
options: Keep feeding both the building and the power company's lines
Raise its output voltage to make up for the lost supply
Switch off by itself so that it cannot feed the lines
Start the standby generator so that the lights stay on

questions.stem: After heavy rain, a solar inverter shows an 'isolation' or low insulation fault. What is the likely cause?
options: The solar panels are producing too much power
The power company's voltage has become too steady
Water in a DC connector or a damaged cable
The inverter's clock needs to be reset

questions.stem: A new office needs 12 more socket circuits for computers. Before adding them to the existing board, what must you check?
options: That the office manager likes the look of the new sockets
That all of the computers are made by the same company
That the new circuits use the same colour of cable
Spare ways, sub-main capacity and the load balance

questions.stem: A sub-main 25 m long carries 40 A. The cable data gives 3 mV per amp per metre. What is the voltage drop?
options: 3 V

questions.stem: A long 220 V feeder to a pump house loses 11 V at full load. As a percentage of the supply, how large is this drop?
The authorised person's clamp meter readings show L1 at 62 A and L2 at 30 A on a 110/220 V board. What should you plan?
options: Move some 110 V circuits from L1 to L2 at an outage
Fit a larger main breaker so that L1 does not trip
Move all the 220 V circuits so they use L1 only
Disconnect the neutral to stop it running hot

questions.stem: During periodic testing of distribution circuits, the authorised person tests each GFCI (RCD) with an RCD tester. What does this test show?
options: That the GFCI's case is the right colour to match the rest of the board
That it trips within its rated time at its rated current
That the cable insulation is still in good condition
That the circuit has been wired with correct polarity

questions.stem: During maintenance you find that a board's circuit schedule no longer matches its circuits. What should you do?
options: Leave it as it is, because the circuits still work
Take the schedule out so that nobody is misled
Trace and confirm the circuits, then update it
Ask the office cleaner which breaker does what

questions.stem: Why are separate final circuits often used for an office's computers instead of sharing with kettles and heaters?
options: So that the computers use less electricity each month
So that the heaters can be run on a 110 V supply
So that the computers do not need an earth at all
To limit disturbances and nuisance trips

questions.stem: A GFCI (RCD) protecting a circuit with many computers trips now and then, but no fault is found. What is a likely cause?
options: The computers are switched off every night
The circuit cable is a larger size than needed
The computers are all the same model
Small normal leakage from each computer adds up

questions.stem: Why should all earthing in a building with electronic equipment go to one main earthing terminal, not to separate 'clean' earth rods?
options: Separate earth rods make the computers run faster
One terminal means fewer earth rods to buy
Separate earths can have voltages between them in a fault or surge
Electronic equipment does not need any earth

questions.stem: A new server rack is installed in a small room with no air conditioning. What is the main risk?
options: The rack will become too heavy for the floor
Heat will shorten equipment life and cause shutdowns
The network cables will stretch and get longer in the heat
The supply frequency in the room will change

questions.stem: A UPS is rated 3 000 VA and 2 400 W. The loads to be connected total 2 600 W. What is the problem?
options: The load is more than the UPS's watt rating
The load is too small for the UPS to start up
The VA rating is too high for these loads
None, because 2 600 is less than 3 000

questions.stem: Why are the cooling filters and heatsinks of VSDs and inverters cleaned during maintenance?
options: So that the display looks clean for the client
Blocked airflow makes them overheat and trip
So that the drive draws more power from the supply
So that the drive's parameters are reset to default

questions.stem: A VSD has run for many years in a hot room. Which parts inside it usually age first and are on the maker's replacement list?
options: The screws that hold the front cover on
The rubber feet under the drive's case
The printed labels on the front panel
The DC bus capacitors and the cooling fans

questions.stem: A failed VSD has been replaced with a new one of the same model. What must be done before the motor is run?
options: Nothing, because the new drive copies the old one by itself
Run the motor at full speed straight away to check it
The authorised person loads the recorded parameters
Set every parameter in the drive to zero

questions.stem: Why should a copy of each VSD's parameter settings be kept with the maintenance records?
options: So a replacement drive can be set up quickly and correctly
So the drive can be sold on later with all of its settings in place
So the client can change them without any training
So the drive's warranty period is doubled

questions.stem: After a lightning storm, several electronic devices in a hotel have failed. Which items should be inspected first?
options: The hotel's roof paint and its rain gutters
The light bulbs in each of the guest rooms
The SPDs and the earthing and bonding
The thermostats of the water heaters

questions.stem: LED fittings with separate drivers are to be installed in a hot ceiling space. What should you check in the driver's data?
options: Its maximum working temperature and output current
Its colour and the shape of its plastic case
Whether it can be painted to match the ceiling
Whether it can safely run with no load at all

questions.stem: LED lamps flicker when a client's old dimmer switch is used. What is the most likely cause?
options: The lamps have been fitted on a 220 V circuit
The dimmer is not compatible with those LED lamps
The dimmer has been wired with too much cable
The lamps are too bright for the size of the room

questions.stem: Why are commercial distribution circuits given periodic inspection and testing, as well as testing when new?
options: The power company charges a fee for each inspection
Cables get thicker and stiffer as they get older
Breakers need resetting by hand every year
Wear, damage, changes and loose joints develop over time

questions.stem: You supervise a trainee wiring a VSD's control cable. Which mistake would you look for first?
options: Signal wires run right alongside the motor cable
Cable labels printed in capital letters
Cable tie tails cut off flush and neat
Cores dressed neatly along the trunking

questions.stem: Why must trainees never take measurements inside a VSD while it is energised?
options: The drive's display will go blank and lose its data
The maker's warranty on the drive will come to an end
The motor will start turning in the wrong direction
The high DC voltages inside it can kill

questions.stem: Which records should be updated after a new circuit is added to a distribution board?
options: The client's list of staff phone numbers
The circuit schedule, test results and drawings
The trainee's attendance record for the week
The breaker maker's catalogue and price list

questions.stem: A client wants you to fit a cheap VSD bought online with no maker's details. What is the best advice?
options: Fit it, because all drives are much the same inside
Fit it, and skip reading its manual to save time
Check its ratings, approval marks and manual first
Refuse to discuss anything further with the client

questions.stem: At handover of a VSD installation, what should the operator be shown?
options: How to change any of the drive's parameters freely whenever they like
How to start, stop and isolate it, and what alarms mean
How to open the drive's cover while it is running
How to bypass the drive's trips when they happen

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: A 4-pole motor is fed at 40 Hz. Using n = 120 × f ÷ p, what is its synchronous speed in rpm?
A fan runs at 50% speed on a VSD. If its power varies with speed cubed, what percentage of full power does it use?
What do the letters EMC stand for?
A 24 V DC supply feeds 8 relays drawing 0.05 A each and a controller drawing 0.6 A. What is the total current, in amps?
A sub-main 20 m long carries 50 A. The cable data gives 4 mV per amp per metre. What is the voltage drop, in volts?
What is the name of the starter that ramps up a motor's voltage smoothly but does not control its running speed?
On a bag that holds a circuit card, what do the letters ESD stand for?
What is the name of the safety feature that stops a grid-tied inverter feeding the lines when the mains fails?
What word describes the distorted currents, at multiples of the supply frequency, drawn by electronic loads such as computers and drives?
What are the stored settings in a VSD, such as motor data, ramp times and limits, called?
A UPS is rated 2 000 VA with a power factor of 0.8. What is its rating in watts?
What is the name of the time a VSD takes to bring the motor from standstill up to its set speed?
What type of cable, with a metal braid or foil round its cores, is used between a VSD and its motor?
A 220 V circuit has a voltage drop of 8.8 V. What percentage of the supply voltage is that?
Which instrument does the authorised person use to check that a GFCI (RCD) trips within its rated time?

essays.stem: Describe how you would plan and install a VSD for a 3.7 kW fan motor in a factory, so that it is safe and does not cause interference with other equipment.
essays.modelAnswer: I would read the drive maker's manual and check that the drive's rating suits the motor's nameplate and the supply. I would choose a mounting place that is clean, dry and cool, keeping the maker's clearances for airflow, and derate or add cooling if the room is hot. The supply would come through a lockable isolator and the protective devices the manual gives. The motor cable would be a screened cable, with its screen clamped all round in EMC glands at both ends, and kept as short as practical. Control and signal cables would be screened too, run apart from the motor and supply cables, and cross them at right angles. All metal parts and the drive would be earthed to the main earthing system. Work is done with the supply isolated, locked off, tagged and proved dead. Before commissioning, I would test insulation resistance of the motor and cable with the cable disconnected from the drive, then do continuity and polarity checks. The authorised person enters the parameters and runs the fan, and I record the settings.
markingPoints: Checks the manual, drive rating, motor nameplate and supply
Chooses a cool, clean place with maker's clearances; derates if hot
Uses screened motor cable with 360° EMC glands at both ends and segregates control cables
Earths correctly and works with the supply isolated and proved dead
Insulation tests with the drive disconnected; parameters and first run by the authorised person; records settings

essays.stem: Explain how a VSD controls the speed of an induction motor, and show with figures why a VSD can save energy on a pump or fan running at 80% speed.
essays.modelAnswer: A VSD first rectifies the incoming AC supply into DC, which is stored on the DC bus capacitors. An inverter stage then switches this DC very quickly to make a new AC output whose frequency and voltage can be changed. The motor's speed depends on the supply frequency, as n = 120 × f ÷ p. For a 4-pole motor at 50 Hz, n = 120 × 50 ÷ 4 = 1 500 rpm; at 40 Hz it is 1 200 rpm, which is 80% of full speed. For fans and centrifugal pumps, the power needed varies roughly with the cube of the speed. At 80% speed, the power is about 0.8 × 0.8 × 0.8 = 0.51, about half of full power. If the flow is controlled by a damper or valve instead, the motor still runs at full speed and wastes energy. So running at 80% speed with a VSD can roughly halve the energy used, which saves money and reduces wear.
markingPoints: Explains rectifier, DC bus and inverter stages
States that speed depends on frequency and uses n = 120 × f ÷ p correctly
Shows that 40 Hz gives 80% speed for a 4-pole motor
Applies the cube law correctly (about 51% power)
Compares with damper or valve control and explains the saving

essays.stem: Describe a maintenance routine for the VSDs, soft starters and control power supplies in a factory, and explain why each task matters.
essays.modelAnswer: I would follow each maker's manual for tasks and intervals. Some checks are done by the authorised person with the equipment running: reading the drive's fault log and running hours, and checking fan operation and temperatures, because the history shows problems early. The other tasks are done with the equipment isolated, locked off, tagged and proved dead, and with the time on the drive's label allowed for the DC bus to discharge, checked with an approved tester. Dust is vacuumed out and filters cleaned or changed, because blocked airflow causes overheating and trips. Terminals are checked to the maker's torque, because vibration and heat loosen them. Cooling fans and DC bus capacitors are replaced at the intervals the maker gives, because they wear out with heat and time. Screens, glands and earth connections are checked for corrosion. Before any card is touched, ESD precautions are used. Parameter settings are backed up and kept with the records. Everything is recorded so trends can be seen.
markingPoints: Follows makers' manuals; live checks of logs, fans and temperatures only by the authorised person
Isolates, proves dead and waits for the DC bus to discharge
Cleans dust and filters and explains overheating
Checks torque, earths and screens; replaces fans and capacitors at set intervals
Uses ESD precautions, backs up parameters and keeps records

essays.stem: Explain how surge protection and earthing work together to protect electronic equipment in a building in Jamaica, and what you would check during maintenance.
essays.modelAnswer: Lightning strikes and switching on the grid can send short, very high voltage surges into a building. Surge protective devices divert the surge current to earth and limit the voltage the equipment sees. An SPD at the main board takes most of the energy, and further SPDs near sensitive equipment, such as computers and alarm panels, reduce what is left. They only work well if their leads are short and straight and the earthing system is sound, because the surge current must reach earth with as little voltage as possible. All earths and bonding should go to one main earthing terminal, so that no large voltage appears between different metal parts or equipment. Data and phone lines entering the building also need surge protection. During maintenance, I would check each SPD's status indicator and replace any that show end of life, check lead lengths and connections, test the continuity of earthing and bonding conductors with the system isolated, and inspect after storms. I would record the checks.
markingPoints: Explains where surges come from and how SPDs divert them
Explains staged protection (main board and near equipment)
Explains short leads, a sound earth and one main earthing terminal
Mentions protection on data and phone lines
Maintenance: status indicators, connections, earthing continuity tests, checks after storms, records

essays.stem: An office in New Kingston is adding 10 computer workstations. The sub-main to its board is 35 m long, protected at 63 A, and the cable data gives 2.5 mV per amp per metre. The new maximum demand will be 55 A at 220 V. The specification allows a 4% voltage drop on the sub-main. Check the sub-main and explain how you would plan the new circuits.
essays.modelAnswer: First the current: the new demand of 55 A is below the 63 A protective device, so the sub-main can carry it if its cable is rated for 63 A. The voltage drop is 2.5 × 55 × 35 = 4 812.5 mV, about 4.8 V. The limit is 4% of 220 V = 8.8 V, so the drop of 4.8 V (about 2.2%) is acceptable. I would then check the board has enough spare ways, or plan a larger board. The workstations would go on separate final circuits from kettles, heaters and the photocopier, to reduce disturbances. Because computers have small normal leakage currents, I would not put too many on one GFCI (RCD), and would share them over several GFCI-protected circuits so one trip does not stop the whole office. I would balance the new 110 V circuits between L1 and L2, fit surge protection, and label everything. Work would be done with safe isolation at an agreed time, then dead tests, live tests by the authorised person, and updated schedules and records.
markingPoints: Checks the demand against the 63 A protection
Calculates the voltage drop (about 4.8 V) and compares it with 8.8 V
Checks spare ways and plans separate circuits for computers
Spreads computers over several GFCI circuits, balances L1 and L2 and adds surge protection
Safe isolation, tests, labels and updated records

essays.stem: Describe how you would plan and lead the periodic inspection and testing of the distribution circuits in a shopping plaza.
essays.modelAnswer: I would agree the scope with the client: which boards and circuits, how much of each will be tested, and when the outages can happen with least disruption to the shops. I would collect the drawings, schedules and the last test report. The visual inspection comes first: the condition of boards, cables and accessories, signs of heat, damage or corrosion, labels and schedules, and changes since the last test. Then, with each circuit isolated, locked off, tagged and proved dead with a checked tester, my team carries out the dead tests: protective conductor continuity, insulation resistance with sensitive equipment disconnected, and polarity. The live tests, such as GFCI (RCD) trip times and fault loop readings, are done only by the authorised person with the right instrument. Results go on a schedule of test results. Any dangerous fault is made safe and reported at once. I would write a report that lists the findings by priority and recommends repairs and the date of the next inspection.
markingPoints: Agrees scope, sampling and outage times with the client; gathers past records
Visual inspection first
Dead tests with safe isolation by the team
Live tests only by the authorised person
Records results, makes dangers safe, reports with priorities and next inspection date

essays.stem: Explain the hazards of maintaining a rooftop grid-tied solar system on a guest house, and describe how you would carry out the maintenance safely.
essays.modelAnswer: Solar panels produce DC voltage whenever light falls on them, and they cannot be switched off. The DC cables from the panels to the DC isolator stay live in daylight, and a DC arc does not go out as easily as an AC arc. The inverter holds stored charge after it is isolated. There is also the risk of falling from the roof, heat, and fragile roof sheets. The power company's rules apply to grid-tied systems, and the inverter must have working anti-islanding protection. To maintain it, I would plan the job, use safe roof access with fall protection, and follow the maker's isolation order: switch off the AC supply to the inverter, then open and lock the DC isolator, and wait the stated time for the inverter to discharge. I would prove dead on the AC side and check for DC with an approved tester. I would never disconnect DC connectors under load. I would inspect panels, mountings, cables and connectors for damage, water and corrosion, clean panels as the maker says, and record readings and the inverter's fault log.
markingPoints: Explains that panels and DC cables stay live in daylight and DC arcs are hard to stop
Mentions inverter stored charge, roof hazards and the power company's rules
Follows the maker's isolation order, waits, proves dead and checks for DC
Never disconnects DC connectors under load; uses fall protection
Inspects, cleans and records

essays.stem: Explain how computers, LED drivers and speed drives can cause problems in distribution circuits, such as hot neutrals and GFCI nuisance tripping, and what can be done about them.
essays.modelAnswer: Electronic loads use rectifiers and switching circuits, so they draw current in short pulses rather than a smooth wave. These distorted currents contain harmonics. In a three-phase, four-wire system, some harmonic currents do not cancel in the neutral but add up, so the neutral can carry a large current and run hot even when the lines are balanced. Harmonics can also heat transformers and cause nuisance tripping. Most electronic equipment also has filters connected to earth, which let a small leakage current flow all the time. On a circuit with many computers, these leakages add up, and a GFCI (RCD) may trip with no real fault. To deal with this, I would follow the specification for neutral sizing where many electronic loads are fed, spread computers over several GFCI-protected circuits, keep electronic loads on separate circuits from heavy loads, and use filters or drives with built-in reactors as the maker advises. I would check neutral terminations during maintenance, and ask the authorised person to measure neutral currents.
markingPoints: Explains that electronic loads draw distorted (harmonic) currents
Explains how some harmonics add in the neutral and cause heating
Explains filter leakage currents adding up and nuisance GFCI trips
Solutions: neutral sizing as specified, spreading loads over circuits, separate circuits, filters or reactors
Checks neutral connections and measurements by the authorised person

essays.stem: Describe how you would install a 24 V DC power supply and a small controller (PLC) rack in a control panel, from choosing the supply to testing.
essays.modelAnswer: I would add up the 24 V loads: the controller, input and output cards, relays, sensors and indicator lamps, and choose a power supply rated above the total with a margin for future loads, such as 25% or as the specification says. I would mount the supply and the rack on DIN rail where the maker's clearances allow cooling, away from heat sources like contactors and drives. The supply's input is fed through suitable protection, and its earth terminal is connected. The 24 V outputs are split into protected groups with fuses or circuit protectors, so one fault does not stop everything. Control wiring is run in separate trunking from power wiring, with numbered ferrules and bootlace ferrules. The cards are kept in their anti-static bags until fitted, using an earthed wrist strap. With the panel isolated and proved dead, I would check continuity and polarity of the 24 V wiring and insulation resistance of the power wiring with the electronics disconnected. The authorised person then powers it up and checks the output voltage and the controller's status.
markingPoints: Adds up the loads and sizes the supply with a margin
Mounts with clearances, away from heat, with input protection and earth connected
Splits outputs into protected groups and segregates and labels the wiring
Uses ESD precautions for the cards
Dead tests with electronics disconnected; power-up and checks by the authorised person

essays.stem: A VSD on a water pump at a hotel has failed with a burnt smell. Describe how you would make it safe, find out why it failed, and return the pump to service.
essays.modelAnswer: I would isolate the drive at its supply isolator, lock off and tag it, then wait at least the time on the drive's label for the DC bus to discharge. I would prove dead at the input terminals with a tester checked before and after, and check the DC bus terminals with the approved tester to confirm no voltage remains. I would read the fault log if the authorised person can retrieve it, and inspect the drive for burnt parts, dust, blocked fans and signs of water or insects. I would also check the cause outside the drive: disconnect the motor cable and test the motor and cable insulation resistance, check the room temperature and the drive's cooling, and look for signs of a surge, such as a failed SPD. Once the cause is found and corrected, the drive is replaced with the same model or an approved equal, wired to EMC practice, and the authorised person loads the saved parameters and runs the pump. I would record the failure, the cause and the actions to stop it happening again.
markingPoints: Isolates, locks off and tags, waits for discharge and proves dead with a checked tester
Reads the fault log and inspects the drive
Checks external causes: motor and cable insulation, cooling, surges
Corrects the cause, replaces like for like and the authorised person restores parameters and runs it
Records the failure, cause and preventive actions

practical1.title: Install a speed drive and motor to EMC good practice, then commission it with the instructor and check speed against frequency
practical1.brief: The assessor provides a training panel with a VSD (or the Centre's equivalent drive), a lockable isolator and a small motor on the bench, with the drive maker's manual and the motor nameplate. The panel is not connected to a supply while the group works; only the instructor energises it. As a group: (1) check that the drive suits the motor and supply, and write down the motor data the drive will need; (2) plan the layout: maker's clearances, cable routes with the motor cable apart from control cables, and gland positions; (3) mount and wire the drive with screened motor cable, clamping the screen all round in EMC glands or clamps at both ends, and wire a start/stop and speed control circuit with numbered ferrules; (4) earth all metal parts; (5) with the motor cable disconnected from the drive, test insulation resistance of the motor and cable, then reconnect and do continuity checks; (6) the instructor energises the panel and enters the parameters while the group watches, then runs the motor at four frequencies (for example 20, 30, 40 and 50 Hz) and reads the speed from the drive's display; the group records the readings in a table beside the speeds worked out with n = 120 × f ÷ p; and (7) write a short commissioning record with the parameters, the test results and the table. Each member wires or tests at least one part and works out one row of the table. Photograph each stage and hand in the commissioning record.
materials: Training panel with a speed drive, lockable isolator and a small motor (switched only by the instructor)
Drive maker's manual and motor nameplate data
Screened motor cable, EMC glands or screen clamps, control cable, numbered and bootlace ferrules
Start/stop push-buttons and a speed potentiometer or selector
Insulation resistance tester and low-resistance ohmmeter
Two-pole voltage tester and proving unit, lock and tag
Commissioning record form and a calculator
photos: The drive and motor data checks written out
The layout plan with cable routes
The screen clamped in the EMC gland at the drive and at the motor
The control wiring with ferrules, kept apart from the motor cable
The insulation resistance test with the motor cable disconnected from the drive
The instructor's test run, with the group's frequency and speed table
checklist: Checked the drive against the motor and supply correctly
Kept the maker's clearances and separated motor and control cables
Terminated the screen correctly at both ends and earthed all metal parts
Wired the control circuit neatly to the drawing with numbered ferrules
Disconnected the drive before the insulation test and tested correctly
Worked out speeds with n = 120 × f ÷ p correctly and compared them with the readings
Stood clear and followed the instructor's directions during the run
safety: Only the instructor energises the panel and changes drive parameters
After the panel is switched off, wait the time on the drive's label before anyone opens it, and prove dead
Keep the motor shaft guard on; stay behind the marked line while it runs
Never insulation-test through the drive; disconnect its output first

practical2.title: Plan, install and test an office sub-board with surge protection and GFCI-protected computer circuits
practical2.brief: The assessor gives the group a brief for an office: a list of loads (computers, printers, a kettle, lights and an air conditioner), the length of the sub-main and cable data, and the training bay with a sub-board to be fitted. The bay is never connected to a supply during the task. As a group: (1) work out the maximum demand, check the sub-main's voltage drop against the limit the assessor gives, and decide the circuits: computers on separate circuits spread over more than one GFCI (RCD), heavy loads on their own circuits, and 110 V circuits balanced between L1 and L2; (2) write the circuit schedule; (3) with the bay isolated, locked off, tagged and proved dead with a tester checked before and after, mount the sub-board and fit the breakers, GFCIs and an SPD with short, straight leads; (4) wire the final circuit tails and the sub-main, with the neutral and earth bars kept separate in the sub-board; (5) carry out dead tests (protective conductor continuity, insulation resistance with the SPD disconnected as its maker says, and polarity) and record them; (6) the instructor tests the GFCIs with an RCD tester while the group records the trip times; and (7) label the board and hand in the calculations, schedule and test record. Each member installs or tests at least one part and writes one part of the documents. Photograph each stage.
materials: Training bay with sub-board (not connected to any supply)
Load list, sub-main length and cable data from the assessor
Breakers, GFCIs (RCDs) and an SPD to suit the board
Cable for the sub-main and final circuit tails, lugs and ferrules
Low-resistance ohmmeter and insulation resistance tester
Two-pole voltage tester and proving unit, lock, hasp and tags
Circuit schedule, test record and label materials
photos: The demand, voltage drop and balance calculations
The bay locked off and proved dead
The sub-board with breakers, GFCIs and the SPD fitted, showing short SPD leads
The separate neutral and earth bars and the terminated tails
The dead tests and completed test record, with the instructor's GFCI trip times
checklist: Worked out the demand and voltage drop correctly and drew the right conclusion
Planned circuits sensibly: computers spread over GFCIs, heavy loads separate, 110 V circuits balanced
Isolated, locked off, tagged and proved dead correctly
Fitted the SPD with short, straight leads and kept neutral and earth bars separate
Terminated conductors neatly to the maker's torque
Carried out and recorded the dead tests correctly
Completed the schedule and labels accurately
safety: The bay is never connected to a supply; only the instructor energises anything and does the GFCI tests
Disconnect the SPD and any electronics before insulation resistance testing, as the makers say
Wear safety glasses when stripping and cutting cable
Keep the board locked off until all work and dead tests are complete
